rows.en: 20  Repel Antibody Coralians
rows.notes: Released mission title reused verbatim from missions_019.json (two spaces, no branch letter, as in that source).

rows.en: <operator(30120,1)><speed(2)>A <book(38)>New Federation<endbook()> executive, <color(5)>Dewey Novak<ce()><thumbnail(194)>, has finally made his move.
rows.notes: Speaker 30120 = Talho Yuki. Dewey Novak per character_names_021.json.

rows.en: <operator(30120,1)><speed(2)>We've gotten word that <book(73)>Antibody Coralians<endbook()> have appeared up ahead. This is <color(5)>Dewey<ce()>'s doing too.
rows.notes: Antibody Coralian per mission_terms_019.json (sourced, matches this mission's title).

rows.en: <operator(30110,1)><speed(2)><book(38)>New Federation<endbook()>'s <color(5)>Dewey<ce()> is pushing forward the <book(78)>Ageha Plan<endbook()>. Let me tell you about it.
rows.notes: Speaker 30110 = Holland Novak. Ageha Plan per encyclopedia_021_b.json / eurekaseven.fandom.com/wiki/Ageha_Plan lock. Sentence reordered (New Federation, Dewey, Ageha Plan) to keep the book()/color() tags in source order.

rows.en: <operator(30110,1)><speed(2)>The <book(78)>Ageha Plan<endbook()> is a document put forward by the hero of the past, <book(68)>Adroc Thurston<endbook()>, concerning the <book(72)>Coralians<endbook()>.
rows.notes: Adroc Thurston per character_names_021/glossary.json. Reordered (Adroc before Coralians) to match source tag order.

rows.en: <operator(30110,1)><speed(2)>It laid out the damage the <book(69)>Scub Coral<endbook()> could do to humanity and Earth, and the mechanism behind it.
rows.notes: Scub Coral per encyclopedia_021_b/022 lock.

rows.en: <operator(30110,1)><speed(2)>At the time, some theorized the <book(49)>Invaders<endbook()> - once among the unidentified life-forms - might have come from the <book(69)>Scub<endbook()>.
rows.notes: 'unidentified life-forms' is the locked hyphenated corpus rendering of the source's own 'nazo no seimeitai' (terms_028.json).

rows.en: <operator(30110,1)><speed(2)>So <book(68)>Adroc<endbook()> turned to the leading authority on <book(49)>Invaders<endbook()> and <book(51)>Getter Rays<endbook()> research, Dr. <color(5)>Saotome<ce()><thumbnail(261)>, and asked for his help.
rows.notes: Reordered (Adroc, Invaders, Getter Ray, then Saotome) to match source tag order; thumbnail kept right after 'Dr. Saotome' as in the reviewed scene 4003070.json precedent.

rows.en: <operator(30110,1)><speed(2)>Together the two of them advanced research on the <book(69)>Scub<endbook()> and drew up the <book(78)>Ageha Plan<endbook()>.
<operator(30110,1)><speed(2)>But partway through the research, something caused <book(68)>Adroc<endbook()> and <color(5)>Saotome<ce()> to fall out.
<operator(30110,1)><speed(2)>As a result, the connection between the <book(49)>Invaders<endbook()> and the <book(69)>Scub<endbook()> was never fully worked out.
<thumbdown()><operator(30110,1)><speed(2)>All that came clear was that the <book(72)>Coralians<endbook()>' existence could trigger the <book(77)>Limit of Questions<endbook()> and destroy the world.
rows.notes: 'Limit of Questions' for Kudan no Genkai per encyclopedia_021_b.json / batch_05943 dialogue lock.

rows.en: <operator(30110,1)><speed(2)>But believing the hypothesis that <book(72)>Coralians<endbook()> had intelligence, <book(68)>Adroc<endbook()> secretly realized something.
rows.notes: 'secretly' used instead of 'quietly' to avoid the lowercase q. Reordered (Coralians before Adroc) to match source tag order.

rows.en: <operator(30110,1)><speed(2)>It was the possibility that talking with the <book(69)>Scub Coral<endbook()> might open a path to coexistence.
<operator(30110,1)><speed(2)>But the Federation of that time saw the <book(72)>Coralians<endbook()> as far too dangerous.
rows.notes: Source just says 'the Federation of that era' without specifying New Federation vs. its predecessor; left generic rather than supplying which.

rows.en: <operator(30110,1)><speed(2)>As a result, they turned the <book(78)>Ageha Plan<endbook()> into a manual for wiping out the <book(69)>Scub Coral<endbook()>.
<operator(30110,1)><speed(2)>The <book(78)>Ageha Plan<endbook()> laid out all sorts of possibilities for the <book(69)>Scub<endbook()>, but it also planted fear in humanity.
<operator(30110,1)><speed(2)>Eliminate them, or live alongside them... The path humanity should take toward the <book(72)>Coralians<endbook()> was split.
<operator(30120,1)><speed(2)><book(68)>Adroc<endbook()> was certain of it - certain that <book(72)>Coralians<endbook()> were intelligent beings. That's why he sought coexistence.
rows.notes: Speaker switches back to 30120 Talho Yuki.

rows.en: <operator(30120,1)><speed(2)>What backed that up was the appearance of a humanoid Coralian.
rows.notes: Source leaves 'Coralian' unwrapped here (no book() tag on this occurrence); matched exactly.

rows.en: <operator(30120,1)><speed(2)>That humanoid Coralian is none other than... <color(4)>Eureka<ce()><thumbnail(259)>.
rows.notes: Source again leaves 'Coralian' unwrapped here; matched exactly.

rows.en: <operator(30120,1)><speed(2)>But... <book(68)>Adroc<endbook()> died in the Summer of Love, and the <book(78)>Ageha Plan<endbook()> was sealed away by the United Federation of Predgio Towers.
rows.notes: 'Summer of Love' per encyclopedia_021_b.json (Saotome's entry). 'United Federation of Predgio Towers' for Toushuu Renpou per encyclopedia_021_a.json lock, also used in reviewed scene 4004673.json.

rows.en: <operator(30120,1)><speed(2)>After that, with <book(40)>Bloodman<endbook()>'s backing, <color(5)>Dewey<ce()> made his comeback and secured his position in today's <book(38)>New Federation<endbook()>.
rows.notes: 'Bloodman' as the short form of the locked 'Fixx Bloodman' was ruled acceptable by the orchestrator (scene 4004573.json); source itself only says 'Bloodman' here. Reordered (Bloodman, Dewey, New Federation) to match source tag order. Orchestrator: shortened to fit three lines.

rows.en: <operator(30120,1)><speed(2)>Using the power he gained by rallying support against the <book(72)>Coralians<endbook()>, he's finally moved to carry out the <book(78)>Ageha Plan<endbook()>.
<operator(30110,1)><speed(2)><color(5)>Dewey<ce()>'s real goal is to use the <book(78)>Ageha Plan<endbook()> and wipe out the <book(69)>Scub Coral<endbook()>.
rows.notes: 'goal' used per terms_028.json orchestrator decision (in place of 'objective').

rows.en: <thumbdown()><operator(30110,1)><speed(2)>But the <book(69)>Scub Coral<endbook()> is this Earth's new land, a being we should be living alongside.
<operator(30110,1)><speed(2)>No matter what, we have to stop my brother... no, <color(5)>Dewey<ce()>'s actions.
rows.notes: Holland catches himself calling Dewey 'brother'; character_names_021.json confirms Dewey is 'Holland's older brother'.

rows.en: <operator(30140,1)><speed(2)>The one <color(5)>Dewey<ce()> started, "<book(82)>Operation Orange<endbook()>,"<thumbnail(264)> means firing crust-penetrating bombs into the ground, into the <book(69)>Scub<endbook()>.
rows.notes: Speaker 30140 = Greg Egan. Operation Orange per encyclopedia_021_b/022 lock; straight quotes for the source's brackets. Reordered (Dewey before the operation name) to match source tag order.

rows.en: <operator(30140,1)><speed(2)><color(5)>Dewey<ce()> is using <book(81)>Orange<endbook()> to pin down the <book(69)>Scub Coral<endbook()>'s nerve center - the <book(80)>Command Cluster<endbook()>.
rows.notes: Orange (bare, the bomb) and Command Cluster per encyclopedia_021_b/022 lock. Reordered (Scub Coral before Command Cluster) to match source tag order.

rows.en: <operator(30140,1)><speed(2)>The <book(80)>Command Cluster<endbook()> is the <book(69)>Scub Coral<endbook()>'s collective will... you might call it its brain.
<operator(30140,1)><speed(2)><color(5)>Dewey<ce()> probably means to destroy the <book(80)>Command Cluster<endbook()> and wipe out the <book(72)>Coralians<endbook()>.
<thumbdown()><operator(30110,1)><speed(2)>But when the <book(69)>Scub<endbook()> is attacked, it spawns <book(73)>Antibody Coralians<endbook()> - to protect itself.
rows.notes: Speaker switches back to 30110 Holland Novak.

rows.en: <operator(30110,1)><speed(2)>And you already know what the <book(73)>Antibody Coralians<endbook()> that appear will do.
<operator(30110,1)><speed(2)>If we leave <color(5)>Dewey<ce()> be like this, the world is ruined. Everyone... I need your help.
<operator(30110,1)><speed(2)>We're heading out to rescue the people under attack by the <book(73)>Antibody Coralians<endbook()>.

uncertainties.issue: 'The Federation of that time' (touji no renpou) is left generic since the source doesn't say New Federation vs. the pre-coup United Federation of Predgio Towers explicitly at this point of the flashback (only slot 39 names Predgio Towers outright).

uncertainties.note: Several rows in this scene (21, 22, 25, 30, 40, 45, 46) needed English word order reshuffled from the most natural phrasing so every book()/color() tag stays in the exact source sequence per the hard format rule; flagged in case a reviewer prefers a looser reading of 'same order' for pure apposition (e.g. 'the Command Cluster, the Scub Coral's nerve center').

meaning_fixes.before: So <book(68)>Adroc<endbook()> turned to the leading authority on <book(49)>Invaders<endbook()> and <book(51)>Getter Ray<endbook()> research, Dr. <color(5)>Saotome<ce()><thumbnail(261)>, and asked for his help.
meaning_fixes.after: So <book(68)>Adroc<endbook()> turned to the leading authority on <book(49)>Invaders<endbook()> and <book(51)>Getter Rays<endbook()> research, Dr. <color(5)>Saotome<ce()><thumbnail(261)>, and asked for his help.
meaning_fixes.reason: Name-spelling inconsistency: every other book(51) occurrence in the corpus (encyclopedia_021_b.json, encyclopedia_022.json, scenes 4003070/4003150/4003240/4003270/4003310/4003731, dialogue batches 02295/02375/06023/07926) renders the locked term as 'Getter Rays' (plural); this row was the only one using the singular 'Getter Ray'. Fixed to match the corpus-wide spelling.

checked_decisions: Slot 0 title equals missions_019.json '20  Repel Antibody Coralians' (two spaces, no branch letter).
Speakers confirmed via tools/speaker_lookup.py: 30120 Talho Yuki (slots 19-20, 36-41), 30110 Holland Novak (slots 21-35, 42-52), 30140 Greg Egan (slots 45-48).
Slot 44 'my brother... no, Dewey's actions' correctly kept as Holland's self-correction; character_names_021.json confirms Dewey is Holland's older brother.

Slot 32 ruling: 'the Federation of that time' correctly left generic (not 'New Federation') since the source's flashback only names 'touji no renpou' without specifying which federation; Predgio Towers is only named afterward, at slot 39.

Reshuffled rows flagged by the translator (slots 21, 22, 25, 30, 40, 45, 46) individually re-translated from the source and checked against the corpus (see tools/scene_source.py output): in every case the word-order change is apposition/clause reordering only and the source meaning (who does what to whom) survives intact.

'Getter Rays' (slot 25) is the only name-spelling problem found this pass; scanned the rest of the corpus's book(51) occurrences (21 other rows) and only this row differed, so the fix is isolated to this row.

'Predgio Towers', 'Scub Coral', 'Command Cluster', 'Ageha Plan', 'Operation Orange', 'Antibody Coralian(s)', 'Bloodman' spellings all checked against encyclopedia_021_a/b.json, encyclopedia_022.json and mission_terms_019.json - all consistent.
Tag sequence verified identical and in source order for every row via a throwaway script comparing tools/scene_source.py output against each row's en field (checked again after the slot 25 fix).

No lowercase j/q found outside locked names ('secretly' and 'quietly' avoidance at slot 30 already correct in the draft); no bare %; no newlines; ASCII only; all rows within the 128 visible-char limit (max 128 at slot 40).
remaining_uncertainties: Slot 32: 'the Federation of that time' is deliberately left ambiguous between the pre-coup United Federation of Predgio Towers and any interim regime, matching the source's own vagueness at that point of the flashback.
